theme: 教材字彙・中高階 750–850 第 53 群

items.pos: adv. 技術上地；嚴格來說
items.colloc: technically speaking 嚴格來說 | technically possible 技術上可行
items.distinct: practically 實際上 | theoretically 理論上
ex: The software is technically compatible with our system.
該軟體技術上與我們的系統相容。
Technically speaking, the contract expired yesterday.
嚴格來說，合約昨天就到期了。
This device is technically difficult to manufacture.
這項裝置在技術上很難製造。

items.pos: adj. 透明的；公開的；易懂的
items.colloc: transparent process 透明的流程 | highly transparent 高度透明
items.distinct: translucent 半透明的 | clear 清楚的
ex: We aim for a transparent hiring process.
我們致力於公開透明的招聘流程。
The company policy lacks transparent communication.
公司政策缺乏透明的溝通。
Management insists on transparent financial reporting.
管理層堅持財務報告要透明。

items.pos: v. 卸下；退貨；傾銷
items.colloc: unload the cargo 卸貨 | unload a truck 卸下卡車
items.distinct: load 裝載 | offload 卸載
ex: The workers started to unload the supplies.
工人們開始卸下物資。
It takes two hours to unload the ship.
卸下這艘船的貨物需要兩小時。
Drivers must unload items at the designated bay.
司機必須在指定區域卸貨。

items.pos: n. 價值；價格 | v. 重視；估價
items.colloc: add value 增加價值 | good value 物超所值
items.distinct: price 價格 | worth 價值（內在）
ex: Our clients value our commitment to quality.
客戶重視我們對品質的承諾。
This service provides great value for money.
這項服務非常物超所值。
We need to add value to our products.
我們需要為產品增加價值。

items.pos: n. 方法；路徑；方向
items.colloc: in a way 在某種程度上 | by way of 經由
items.distinct: method 方法（較正式） | approach 手段
ex: There is no easy way to solve this.
沒有簡單的方法解決這個問題。
Please suggest a better way to proceed.
請建議一個更好的進行方式。
We found a new way to reduce costs.
我們找到一個降低成本的新方法。

items.pos: v. 廣播；播放 | n. 廣播節目
items.colloc: broadcast live 現場直播 | news broadcast 新聞廣播
items.distinct: transmit 傳送 | announce 宣佈
ex: The company will broadcast the seminar online.
公司將在網路上直播研討會。
This message is broadcast to all employees.
這則訊息已向全體員工廣播。
The news broadcast starts at six sharp.
新聞廣播在六點準時開始。

items.pos: adv. 粗心地；不小心地
items.colloc: act carelessly 行事粗心 | handle carelessly 粗心處理
items.distinct: negligently 疏忽地 | recklessly 魯莽地
ex: He carelessly left the important file open.
他粗心地把重要檔案開著。
Data was carelessly entered into the system.
資料被粗心地輸入到系統中。
Do not handle the fragile equipment carelessly.
不要粗心處理易碎設備。

items.pos: v. 追逐；追趕 | n. 追逐
items.colloc: chase potential clients 爭取潛在客戶 | wild goose chase 白費力氣
items.distinct: pursue 追求（目標） | track 追蹤
ex: Sales teams often chase new business leads.
業務團隊常爭取新的商業線索。
We spent all day chasing missing invoices.
我們花了一整天追蹤遺失的發票。
He is chasing a promotion this year.
他今年正追求升遷。

items.pos: n. 情況；境遇；情勢
items.colloc: under the circumstances 在這種情況下 | due to circumstances 由於情況
items.distinct: situation 處境 | condition 條件
ex: Under the circumstances, we must cancel the trip.
在這種情況下，我們必須取消行程。
Unforeseen circumstances delayed the project completion.
無法預見的情況延遲了專案完工。
We adapt quickly to changing market circumstances.
我們迅速適應變化的市場情勢。

items.pos: v. 倒塌；崩潰；暴跌 | n. 倒塌；崩潰
items.colloc: financial collapse 財政崩潰 | market collapse 市場崩盤
items.distinct: fail 失敗 | drop 下降
ex: The stock market faced a sudden collapse.
股市面臨了突然的崩盤。
Their negotiations collapsed due to low trust.
由於信任不足，談判破裂了。
The old warehouse might collapse next winter.
那座舊倉庫明年冬天可能會倒塌。

items.pos: n. 混亂；困惑；混淆
items.colloc: cause confusion 造成混亂 | avoid confusion 避免混淆
items.distinct: disorder 雜亂 | misunderstanding 誤解
ex: Lack of instructions caused much confusion.
缺乏說明造成了許多困惑。
We apologize for the confusion regarding dates.
我們對日期方面的混淆深表歉意。
The new policy led to internal confusion.
新政策導致了內部的混亂。

items.pos: v. 建造；構建 | n. 構念
items.colloc: construct a building 蓋建築 | construct a plan 制定計畫
items.distinct: build 蓋（通俗） | establish 建立
ex: They will construct a new office tower.
他們將建造一座新的辦公大樓。
We need to construct a better marketing strategy.
我們需要構建更好的行銷策略。
The team is constructing a test model.
團隊正在構建一個測試模型。

items.pos: n. 曲線；彎曲處 | v. 彎曲
items.colloc: learning curve 學習曲線 | growth curve 成長曲線
items.distinct: arc 弧線 | bent 彎曲的
ex: The graph shows a steep growth curve.
圖表顯示出陡峭的成長曲線。
Mastering this software has a learning curve.
精通這套軟體需要一段學習時間。
The road curves ahead near the office.
辦公室前面的道路轉彎了。

items.pos: v. 擊敗；挫敗 | n. 失敗；擊敗
items.colloc: accept defeat 接受失敗 | suffer a defeat 遭受失敗
items.distinct: failure 失敗（結果） | loss 損失
ex: Our team was defeated in the final round.
我們的團隊在決賽中被擊敗。
They refused to accept defeat so easily.
他們拒絕如此輕易地接受失敗。
The motion was defeated by the board.
該提案被董事會否決了。

items.pos: adj. 令人沮喪的；蕭條的
items.colloc: depressing news 令人沮喪的消息 | depressing atmosphere 悶的氣氛
items.distinct: depressed 感到沮喪的 | sad 悲傷的
ex: The sales report is quite depressing today.
今天的銷售報告相當令人沮喪。
It is depressing to see profits decline.
看到利潤下滑令人感到沮喪。
The office has a depressing atmosphere today.
辦公室今天有一種悶悶的氣氛。

items.pos: adj. 令人失望的
items.colloc: disappointing result 令人失望的結果 | disappointing performance 表現不佳
items.distinct: disappointed 感到失望的 | unsatisfactory 不滿意的
ex: The quarterly results were quite disappointing.
本季的財務結果相當令人失望。
We had a disappointing meeting this morning.
我們今天早上開了一場令人失望的會議。
Such a low turnout is very disappointing.
出席率如此之低非常令人失望。

items.pos: v. 不喜歡；厭惡 | n. 不喜歡
items.colloc: strong dislike 強烈反感 | express dislike 表達不滿
items.distinct: hate 憎恨 | resent 憤恨
ex: I dislike working in a noisy environment.
我不喜歡在吵雜的環境中工作。
Management dislikes constant delays in reporting.
管理層不喜歡報告時常延遲。
She makes her dislike for the plan clear.
她清楚表達了對該計畫的不喜歡。

items.pos: adj. 傑出的；卓越的；著名的
items.colloc: distinguished career 卓越的職業生涯 | distinguished guest 貴賓
items.distinct: famous 著名的 | excellent 極佳的
ex: He has a distinguished career in finance.
他在金融界有著卓越的職業生涯。
We invited a distinguished speaker for today.
我們邀請了一位傑出的演講者。
She received an award for distinguished service.
她因卓越的服務而獲得獎項。

items.pos: v. 支配；主導；佔優勢
items.colloc: dominate the market 主導市場 | dominate the conversation 主導對話
items.distinct: control 控制 | influence 影響
ex: Our firm continues to dominate the market.
我們公司持續主導市場。
The project requirements dominate our time now.
專案需求目前佔用了我們大量的時間。
Large corporations often dominate this industry.
大型企業常在這行業佔據優勢。

items.pos: adv. 有效地；實際上
items.colloc: work effectively 有效地工作 | operate effectively 有效地運作
items.distinct: efficiently 高效率地 | successfully 成功地
ex: We need to communicate more effectively.
我們需要更有效地溝通。
The new policy is effectively in place.
新政策實際上已經生效了。
Managers should lead their teams effectively.
主管應有效地帶領他們的團隊。
